boundary.name: unproved decode wall, weights resident
includes: the forward passes that produce the measured tokens
sampling/argmax, KV-cache growth, the engine's own scheduling
excludes: process start, weight load and any compile/CUDA-graph capture (a warmup pass precedes every timed rep)
tokenization of the prompt (built once, outside the timed region)
the prefill -- for the decode-only rate ONLY; it is measured by a separate max_new_tokens=1 call and subtracted. The e11 rate includes it.
boundary.comparable_to: the proved side's per-chunk boundaries. NOTE: none of the four proved boundaries contains an inference pass -- `whole wall` is trace gen + stwo + serialization, and even `loop_secs`, which adds the witness READ and the layer build, reads a witness that a prior extraction produced. So every ratio here is prover-seconds against inference-seconds, which is exactly the quantity fn. 170 computed (zkLLM's 803 s against 668 tok/s). An end-to-end deployment that must both infer and prove costs (1 + ratio), not (ratio) -- immaterial at x25-40, and stated anyway.

counting_conventions.decode_only: (new_tokens - 1) / decode_s. The v1 comparison: our proved seconds cover only the 512 decoded positions (scope.prefill_status -- the prefix is declared, not proven), so the baseline excludes prefill too. Excluding prefill makes the unproved rate LARGER, so this choice makes the reported overhead LARGER.
counting_conventions.e11: (prompt_tokens + new_tokens) / total_s. Every position of the concatenated prompt+output pass over that pass's whole wall -- the convention DeepProve's TPM uses and the one our own statement needs once E11 proves the prompt. At C=4096 it counts 4608 positions, not 512, so the unproved rate is much larger and the multiple grows with C.

measured.ladder_uses: tok_s_decode_per_stream.median for the single-stream latency row; tok_s_decode_aggregate.median for the batched $/token row; tok_s_e11_all_positions_*.median for the E11 arm

dimensions.name: model
dimensions.note: unsloth/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct @ 4699cc75b550f9c6f3173fb80f4703b62d946aa5; 32 layers, hidden 4096, 32 heads, 8 KV, vocab 128256, bf16.

dimensions.name: tokenizer
dimensions.note: Recorded so a reader can check the token stream is the same one; tok/s is meaningless across two tokenizations.

dimensions.name: card
dimensions.note: The proved row is one GPU. A ratio across two different cards is not an overhead multiple.

dimensions.name: context_keys
dimensions.proved: no proved row at C=1024; the freeze has 4096 and 16384 only
dimensions.note: C is the committed KV prefix (prover `--ctx`); the S=512 decoded positions attend over it plus the causal corner, so the unproved run prompts with exactly C tokens and decodes 512 more.

dimensions.name: new_tokens
dimensions.note: Both sides divide by the same token count. EOS is suppressed so exactly this many are produced.

dimensions.name: decoding
dimensions.note: The argmax gadget proves 'the emitted token is the maximum', strict-lowest-index, tied to the head dequant's own output. A sampled token would need committed randomness plus a CDF check. Whether the published system proves anything about sampling is UNKNOWN from the public record.

dimensions.name: batch_size
dimensions.note: The proved row is one sequence per proof, batch 1. This is the like-for-like latency comparison.

dimensions.name: arithmetic
dimensions.note: We prove a quantized arithmetic; the baseline runs the deployed one. A bf16/fp16 baseline is SLOWER than an int8/fp8 serving stack, so this mismatch makes the overhead multiple we report SMALLER than the truth. Pass --dtype to run a faster baseline arm and the multiple grows.

dimensions.name: positions_counted
dimensions.proved: 512 decoded positions; prompt declared, not proven
dimensions.note: The v1 comparison. The proved seconds never include the prompt, so the unproved rate excludes prefill too (a separate max_new_tokens=1 call, subtracted). The SAME run also records an `e11` rate over all prompt+output positions -- the convention DeepProve's TPM uses -- and the ladder reports it as a separate arm under a named assumption. tok_s_wall (512 positions but prefill included) is recorded and used by neither.
